borne-over.label: Borne over
borne-over.gloss: The verb is motion: a spirit carried above the water (LXX ἐπεφέρετο, Vulgate ferebatur).

wind.label: A wind
wind.gloss: Ruach is weather, not a person; Onkelos keeps God at a remove.

spirit-of-mercy.label: Spirit of mercy
spirit-of-mercy.gloss: A divine disposition blowing over the waters (Palestinian targums).

messiah.label: Spirit of the Messiah
messiah.gloss: Resh Lakish: the ruach of Isa 11:2, brought by repentance-as-water.

bird-hovering.label: Dove hovering, not touching
bird-hovering.gloss: Ben Zoma and Rashi: the bird measures a gap; it does not land.

fluttering.label: Fluttering
fluttering.gloss: Abelard's report of the Hebrew: volitabat, as the eagle of Deut 32:11.

brooding-warmth.label: Bird brooding, warming
brooding-warmth.gloss: Jerome from the Hebrew, Basil's Syrian, then the Latin schools: the Spirit quickens matter like a hen on eggs.

power-not-place.label: Power, not place
power-not-place.gloss: Augustine: 'above' means sovereignty, not position; the Manichees misread it.

craftsman.label: The craftsman's will
craftsman.gloss: The Spirit over the waters as the maker's intention over the wood.

love-gift.label: Love, gift, weight
love-gift.gloss: Confessions XIII: why the Spirit alone is said to be above; pondus meum amor meus.

trinity.label: The Trinity named
trinity.gloss: The verse completes Father (in principio), Son (principium), Spirit.

heart.label: Over the heart
heart.gloss: Isidore's moral reading: the waters are our fluid, dark heart.

throne.label: Throne of Glory
throne.gloss: Rashi: the throne stands in the air, held by the breath of God's mouth.

unus-cardinal.label: The versions keep the cardinal
unus-cardinal.gloss: ἡμέρα μία, dies unus, yoma chad: 'one', not 'first', in every ancient version.

unus-grammatical.label: 'First' needs a second
unus-grammatical.gloss: The series 'one, second, third' is improper (Bereshit Rabbah); or, first and second are relatives and there was no second yet (Bruno).

unus-alone.label: God was alone that day
unus-alone.gloss: Yachid in his world: no angels were made on the first day, so there was no second anything (Bereshit Rabbah, Rashi).

unus-yom-kippur.label: The one day given to Israel
unus-yom-kippur.gloss: 'One day' is the Day of Atonement, the day the Holy One gave them.

unus-24-hours.label: One circuit, twenty-four hours
unus-24-hours.gloss: Day and night together make one revolution, and the whole is named from the day alone.

unus-repeated.label: The same day repeated
unus-repeated.gloss: There is one day only — the angelic light — presented once for each kind of thing made (Augustine).

unus-all-time.label: One day = all time
unus-all-time.gloss: The word holds the whole span of the ages, or the whole work of the six days (Augustine's set-aside reading; Abelard's own).

unus-angelic-unity.label: The unity of angelic dignity
unus-angelic-unity.gloss: 'One' names the undivided attention of the angelic mind, not a place in a series (Angelomus).

unus-eternal-day.label: The true first day is eternal
unus-eternal-day.gloss: This day is first only by number and order of creation; the day that is first by nature is uncreated light (Rupert).

day-precedes-night.label: Day before night
day-precedes-night.gloss: Evening is the end of a finished day, morning the end of the night; days are counted from morning to morning.

day-follows-night.label: Night before day
day-follows-night.gloss: 'One day' rules that reckoning begins at evening (Ben Zoma, b. Chullin 83a).

night-for-rest.label: Night made for rest
night-for-rest.gloss: Day is for labour and night for rest, so only the day's bounds are counted.

day-is-a-measure.label: The day's measure is a creature
day-is-a-measure.gloss: The measure of day and of night was itself made on day one (b. Chagigah 12a).

evening-is-completion.label: Evening completes a work
evening-is-completion.gloss: Vespera is a work perfected, mane the beginning of the next — the Carolingian formula.

evening-is-self-knowledge.label: Evening and morning knowledge
evening-is-self-knowledge.gloss: The creature known in itself is evening; known in the Word and referred back in praise, morning (Augustine).

evening-moral.label: Evening as sin or temptation
evening-moral.gloss: Evening and morning are the deeds of the wicked and the righteous, or sin and renewal, or temptation and the light of justice.

simul.label: All things made at once
simul.gloss: Creavit omnia simul (Sir 18:1): the days are not successive.

six-days-literal.label: Six real days
six-days-literal.gloss: Created at once in matter, distinguished in form through six successive days (the common doctors, Bonaventure).

principio-temporis.label: In the beginning of time
principio-temporis.gloss: The word dates the making: time began with the world, and there was no before (Onkelos, Bede, Rabanus, Remigius, Hugh).

principio-in-filio.label: In the Son
principio-in-filio.gloss: Principium is a proper name of the Word, on the strength of John 8:25 and Ps 104:24 (Ambrose, Augustine, Isidore, Alcuin, the Glossa, Rupert, Honorius).

principio-first-of-all.label: First of all things
principio-first-of-all.gloss: 'In the beginning' means before everything else that follows — in the beginning of the creatures, or on the first day (Augustine's second reading; Bruno, Abelard).

principio-is-first-creature.label: The first creature is a beginning
principio-is-first-creature.gloss: The first intellectual creature may be called a beginning to the things it heads (Augustine, De Genesi imperfectus).

beginning-is-wisdom.label: In Wisdom
beginning-is-wisdom.gloss: The beginning is Wisdom — which is the Torah on one bench (Prov 8:22, Prov 3:19, Neofiti) and the Son on the other (Ps 104:24).

reshit-is-torah.label: The beginning is the Torah
reshit-is-torah.gloss: Reshit is the Torah, called reshit darko: God looked into it as an architect into his plans and created the world (Bereshit Rabbah, Rashi).

reshit-is-israel.label: For the sake of Israel
reshit-is-israel.gloss: Reshit is Israel, called reshit tevu'ato (Jer 2:3); the world was made for their sake.

reshit-construct.label: 'When God began to create'
reshit-construct.gloss: Bereshit is a construct and the verse a subordinate clause: at the beginning of God's creating (Rashi's plain sense, Ibn Ezra; contested by Ramban).

world-has-a-beginning.label: The world is not eternal
world-has-a-beginning.gloss: The point of saying 'in the beginning' at all is that the world had one, against the philosophers (Ambrose, Remigius, Hugh, Ramban).

bereshit-book-name.label: It is the book's name
bereshit-book-name.gloss: The Hebrews name volumes from their opening words, so bresith is the title of Genesis (Jerome, Wigbod, Angelomus).

six-preceded.label: Six things preceded the world
six-preceded.gloss: Torah and the Throne of Glory were made before it; the patriarchs, Israel, the Temple and the Messiah's name were contemplated (Bereshit Rabbah 1:4).

read-it-twice.label: Say the phrase twice
read-it-twice.gloss: In principio is to be repeated — once in the Son, once at the beginning of time — rather than decided (Comestor).

lux-corporalis.label: A bodily light
lux-corporalis.gloss: A material light made to light material things, standing in the sun's place until the fourth day (Basil, Ambrose, Bede, Hugh, Honorius, Comestor, Bonaventure).

lux-angelica.label: The angelic creation
lux-angelica.gloss: The light is the spiritual creature called 'heaven' in v. 1, made light by turning to its Creator (Augustine, Angelomus, Rupert).

lux-hidden.label: Stored for the righteous
lux-hidden.gloss: Too good for the wicked, it was hidden away and is kept for the righteous in the time to come (Bereshit Rabbah, b. Chagigah, Rashi).

lux-garment.label: From the light of his garment
lux-garment.gloss: God wrapped himself in it like a garment (Ps 104:2); the heavens were stretched out of it (Bereshit Rabbah, Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer).

lux-from-temple.label: From the site of the Temple
lux-from-temple.gloss: The light was created from the place of the sanctuary (Ezek 43:2; Jer 17:12).

lux-becomes-luminaries.label: The luminaries were made from it
lux-becomes-luminaries.gloss: The nature of light was made on day one and hung in the firmament on day four (the sages in b. Chagigah 12a; an unnamed opinion in Augustine).

lux-twilight.label: A light like the dawn
lux-twilight.gloss: Not the sun's brightness but what the sky is before sunrise or after sunset (Remigius, Honorius, Comestor, Hugh).

lux-is-day.label: 'Light' just means day
lux-is-day.gloss: The verse answers itself: he called the light Day, so light here is put for day (Bruno).

lux-is-distinction.label: The distinguishing of the works
lux-is-distinction.gloss: The light is the confused heap becoming distinct and knowable, not a thing at all (Abelard).

fiat-is-instantaneous.label: Speaking is making
fiat-is-instantaneous.gloss: No interval between the command and the thing: the Hebrew says only 'let it be, and it was' (Ambrose, Basil, Angelomus, Abelard).

pair-is-formless-matter.label: Unformed matter
pair-is-formless-matter.gloss: The pair names the matter God had made and not yet given form to (Augustine, Angelomus, Hugh, Comestor).

pair-is-under-water.label: Hidden under the waters
pair-is-under-water.gloss: Invisible because the waters covered it, and because there was neither light nor anyone to see (Basil, Alcuin, Angelomus, Ibn Ezra).

pair-is-unfurnished.label: No seed, no living thing
pair-is-unfurnished.gloss: Empty of shoots and void of animals: a list of what was not there yet (Bede, Remigius, Rupert, Abelard, Hugh, Comestor, the targums).

pair-is-a-name-for-us.label: A name fitted to slow minds
pair-is-a-name-for-us.gloss: Not a description but the most serviceable word for formlessness, since earth and the deep are the least comely things men know (Augustine, Confessions XII).

pair-many-senses.label: More than one true reading
pair-many-senses.gloss: Five readings of the clause are all true and none can be shown to be Moses' own (Augustine, Confessions XII.21).

pair-is-two-things.label: A green line and slimy stones
pair-is-two-things.gloss: Tohu and bohu are two creatures made on the first day: a line encircling the world, and stones sunk in the deep (b. Chagigah 12a, Sefer Yetzirah).

pair-is-matter-and-form.label: Matter and its form
pair-is-matter-and-form.gloss: Tohu is the hyle, which can hold no name; bohu is bo hu, the form it puts on (Ramban).

pair-is-astonishment.label: Astonishment
pair-is-astonishment.gloss: Tohu is what astonishes whoever looks at it — the earth bewildered at her lot, or the reader appalled at the emptiness (Bereshit Rabbah 2:2, Rashi, the Bahir).

pair-is-history.label: The verse tells history
pair-is-history.gloss: The clause is the first term of a periodization: the generations from Adam, the four kingdoms, or the Church before her children (Bereshit Rabbah 2:1, 2:3, 2:4; Bruno).

pair-is-our-flesh.label: The earth of our flesh
pair-is-our-flesh.gloss: The soul before it has taken the form of doctrine (Isidore, Wigbod, Rabanus, Remigius, Bruno).

pair-is-not-of-heaven.label: Said of earth, not of heaven
pair-is-not-of-heaven.gloss: The phrase is withheld from heaven, which was filled with angels as soon as it was made (Bede, the Glossa, Angelomus, Abelard).

heaven-first.label: Heaven first
heaven-first.gloss: Beit Shammai: the word order is the order of the acts, and a king has his throne made before its footstool (Isa 66:1).

earth-first.label: Earth first
earth-first.gloss: Beit Hillel: a builder raises the lower storey first (Amos 9:6), and Gen 2:4 and Ps 102:26 name the earth before the heavens.

both-at-once.label: Both together
both-at-once.gloss: The sages, and R. Shimon ben Yoḥai's stewpot and its lid (Isa 48:13); Ambrose, that the order of naming gives heaven no privilege of the firstborn.

order-of-dignity.label: Named for dignity, not order
order-of-dignity.gloss: Heaven stands first because it is worthier, or because the account is about to turn to the earth (Hugh of St Victor; R. Yoḥanan's creation-and-completion).

created-then-stretched.label: Created in one order, stretched in the other
created-then-stretched.gloss: Resh Lakish: heaven was created first, the earth was stretched out first — so both proof-texts stand.

heaven-earth-is-everything.label: A name for the whole creation
heaven-earth-is-everything.gloss: Two visible words standing for all that God made, given so for the weakness of little ones (Augustine, Alcuin, Angelomus, Comestor).

heaven-is-empyrean.label: The empyrean heaven
heaven-is-empyrean.gloss: Not the visible firmament but a fiery — from brightness, not heat — and intellectual heaven, filled with angels as soon as it was made (Remigius, the Glossa, Comestor).

heaven-earth-four-elements.label: The four elements
heaven-earth-four-elements.gloss: Heaven names fire and air, earth names earth and water; the verse announces the material first principles of bodies (Ambrose, Abelard, Ramban, Comestor).

et-includes.label: The particle includes
et-includes.gloss: Et ha-shamayim brings in the sun, moon and constellations; ve-et ha-aretz the trees, the plants and the Garden of Eden (Bereshit Rabbah 1:14, b. Chagigah 12a, Ramban).

shamayim-is-water.label: Sham mayim — 'there is water'
shamayim-is-water.gloss: The name itself says what heaven is made of: water, or fire and water mingled into the firmament (b. Chagigah 12a).

one-earth-only.label: One earth, and no heaven of heavens here
one-earth-only.gloss: If the heavens of v. 1 were the intelligible heaven, the earth beside it could not be the ground; the seven earths are seven regions of the one (Ibn Ezra; Abelard, from the other end).

whole-then-parts.label: The whole first, then the parts
whole-then-parts.gloss: V. 1 is a heading: Scripture commends everything God made in two words before going through it with 'God said' (Augustine, Angelomus, the Glossa).
